title: Programming & Tooling for AI
blurb: The tools every AI engineer reaches for daily: Python, the scientific stack, PyTorch, git, the shell, containers, GPUs, and the data formats that the field has converged on.

nodes.label: Python (real proficiency)
nodes.description: Not just syntax — typing, packaging, virtual environments, async, the standard library, the ecosystem. AI engineering runs on Python; you should be fluent, not survival-level.
nodes.doneWhen: You can read and debug a non-trivial Python codebase (e.g., a small open-source library) without flailing.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial (official docs)
resources.annotation: The single best Python intro. Free, comprehensive, current; the first place to look up anything.

resources.title: Fluent Python (2e)
resources.author: Luciano Ramalho
resources.annotation: The book that turns survival-Python into idiomatic-Python. Iterators, descriptors, async — the parts you actually need on a real codebase.

resources.title: Real Python
resources.annotation: The reference site for focused Python tutorials. Use it when you hit a tooling question (uv, pytest, asyncio) and need the right answer quickly.

nodes.label: NumPy & the scientific stack
nodes.description: NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib. Vectorized thinking, broadcasting, einops, the difference between a column-major and row-major mental model. The substrate for every framework above.
nodes.doneWhen: You can express a small data pipeline in vectorized NumPy without writing a Python for-loop over elements.

resources.title: NumPy: the absolute basics for beginners
resources.annotation: The official intro. Start here; the docs are unusually well-written.

resources.title: From Python to NumPy
resources.author: Nicolas Rougier
resources.annotation: Free online book that drills vectorized thinking. The 'how do I stop writing for-loops?' resource.

resources.title: einops — tensor operations for readable code
resources.annotation: The library that makes tensor reshaping legible. Read the README; you'll start writing rearrange/repeat/reduce within an hour.

nodes.label: PyTorch
nodes.description: The framework. Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, the training loop, GPU placement, distributed basics. TensorFlow exists; in 2026, the practical AI-engineer default is PyTorch.
nodes.doneWhen: You can write a training loop from scratch (no Lightning, no Trainer) for a small model and explain every line.

resources.title: PyTorch — Deep Learning with PyTorch: A 60 Minute Blitz
resources.annotation: The official quickstart. The fastest path from 'I know NumPy' to 'I can train a model'.

resources.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
resources.annotation: Build neural nets in PyTorch from scratch, one micrograd-flavored step at a time. The closest thing to a canonical PyTorch+ML course.

resources.title: Deep Learning with PyTorch
resources.author: Stevens, Antiga, Viehmann
resources.annotation: Free PDF from PyTorch.org. The official book; covers tensors through nn.Module through training in depth.

nodes.label: Git & GitHub workflows
nodes.description: Branches, rebasing, commits-as-units-of-thought, PR reviews, conflict resolution, history that future-you can read. Not optional — every AI engineer reads and contributes to open-source.
nodes.doneWhen: You can rebase a feature branch cleanly, write a useful commit message, and review a PR thoughtfully.

resources.title: Pro Git
resources.author: Scott Chacon
resources.annotation: The free official book. Skim the early chapters, internalize the chapter on branching, and revisit the rebase chapter when you need it.

resources.title: Oh My Git!
resources.annotation: An interactive game that teaches the actual graph model behind branches and merges. The clearest 30 minutes you'll spend on git.

resources.title: How to Write a Git Commit Message
resources.author: Chris Beams
resources.annotation: The seven rules. Re-read whenever your messages start to feel like 'fix stuff'.

nodes.label: Linux, the shell, SSH
nodes.description: The terminal, file permissions, processes, pipes, SSH, screen/tmux, basic networking. You will be on a GPU box more often than you expect.
nodes.doneWhen: You can SSH into a remote GPU machine, set up a Python environment, kick off a training run, and come back to its logs.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
resources.annotation: The shell, tmux, ssh, dotfiles, build systems — everything CS curricula skip. The single best resource.

resources.title: tldr pages
resources.annotation: `man` pages reduced to the five flags you actually use. Install once; reach for it instead of Googling.

resources.title: Bash Guide for Beginners
resources.author: Machtelt Garrels
resources.annotation: The free Linux Documentation Project guide. The right depth when shell scripting goes beyond a one-liner.

nodes.label: Docker & containers
nodes.description: Containers for reproducible environments, Dockerfile basics, image layers, GPU containers. The standard packaging for any model that ships.
nodes.doneWhen: You can write a Dockerfile for a small ML service and explain image layering.

resources.title: Docker — Get Started
resources.annotation: The official guide. Read it once, build the sample app, then your mental model is set.

resources.title: Best practices for writing Dockerfiles
resources.annotation: Layer caching, multi-stage builds, what to put in .dockerignore. The 10 minutes that prevent 4GB images.

resources.title: NVIDIA Container Toolkit
resources.annotation: How to run a CUDA workload inside a container. The bridge you cross the first time you Dockerize a training job.

nodes.label: GPU & CUDA basics
nodes.description: What a GPU is, what VRAM is, what blocks/threads/warps are conceptually, how PyTorch uses CUDA, why memory bandwidth matters. You don't need to write CUDA kernels; you do need to debug OOMs and understand throughput.
nodes.doneWhen: You can diagnose an out-of-memory error and choose batch size + precision intentionally.

resources.title: GPUs Go Brrr
resources.author: Hazy Research (Stanford)
resources.annotation: A vivid, accessible explainer of what makes modern GPUs fast and where the bottlenecks live. The mental model you want.

resources.title: Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles
resources.author: Horace He
resources.annotation: Compute vs memory-bound vs overhead-bound. The single best intro to GPU-shaped performance thinking.

resources.title: PyTorch CUDA semantics
resources.annotation: Device placement, streams, OOM diagnostics. The reference you'll come back to.

nodes.label: Data formats & loading
nodes.description: Parquet, Arrow, the `datasets` library, streaming datasets, sharding. The realities of moving training-scale data around.
nodes.doneWhen: You can stream a multi-GB dataset through a training loop without OOMing the host.

resources.title: Apache Arrow — Format Specification
resources.annotation: Why columnar storage is fast and what Arrow / Parquet are doing under the hood. A short read; useful intuition.

resources.title: Hugging Face Datasets
resources.annotation: The library you'll use to load, stream, and shard training data in practice. Memory-mapped Arrow under the hood.

resources.title: Polars — DataFrames for the modern era
resources.annotation: The Pandas successor most teams reach for in 2026 when data work outgrows Pandas. Lazy, Arrow-native, fast.
